name: Canopy Super App
imageAlt: Canopy Super App: Web3 super app with launchpad, DEX, and chain explorer that scaled to 25K concurrent users at testnet.
description: Founding Frontend Engineer for Canopy Network — zero-to-one architecture for a Web3 super app that held 25K+ concurrent users at testnet launch.
dossier: I joined Canopy Network as Founding Frontend Engineer and owned the end-to-end frontend for a decentralized L1 that lets teams launch nested chains with their own business logic and tokenomics. I designed and shipped the launchpad's user flow, DEX, and chain explorer. The testnet launched with more than 25,000 concurrent users in the first week, and that architecture is still the foundation of the app.

Every foundational decision had to be made from scratch against just a product specification and always fluid PRDs against a fixed launch date. I set the stack — React, Next.js, and Node.js — and sequenced delivery around the products need: launchpad first so teams could discover and create chains, then the DEX, then the explorer for transactions and other  chain and token related data.

I treated blockchain integration, reliability, and SEO as launch constraints, not later work. The frontend stayed stable through testnet traffic at that scale and did not require a rewrite afterward. Most of that original frontend groundwork is still in production.
tasks: Created the frontend for launchpad, DEX, and explorer experience

name: Timothy Sykes
imageAlt: Timothy Sykes: trading-education website with news, quotes, webinars, and a headless Nuxt and WordPress architecture.
description: Lead Full-Stack Engineer for TimothySykes.com — Frontend Architecture and Systems Development for  website serving more than 1M+ monthly users.
dossier: I own the frontend and web services for StocksToTrade, the company's trading-education and market-data platform — charting, scanners, watchlists, webinars, and news. The platform reliably serves around 1M unique monthly users, with hundreds of active users on the site at any given minute.

The site needed to show live stock quotes and market data to that audience without sacrificing performance or reliability. I designed the real-time ingestion pipeline using WebSockets, Node.js, AWS, and NoSQL databases, and made the core architecture decisions for how data flows from source to page. StocksToTrade and TimothySykes.com both depend on the same upstream market-data API, so I put a shared cache and fallback in front of it — one outage no longer breaks quotes on both sites at once, and each site reads live data at request time instead of baking it into a static build.

The editorial and SEO team was manually handling QA checks, SEO integrity checks, and comment moderation — expensive and impossible to scale. I have designed and built LLM-powered automation tooling to take that work off their hands.
tasks: Live stock data ingestion, quotes, and news pipeline
AI automation for QA, SEO, and ops

name: Content automation with AWS, JavaScript, and WordPress
imageAlt: Article: automating featured images for Nuxt and headless WordPress with AWS Lambda, Canvas, and OpenAI.
description: How I automated featured images for a Nuxt + headless WordPress publisher — Lambda, Canvas, and OpenAI instead of a daily CMS chore.
dossier: I was building a Nuxt SSG on headless WordPress for a tech publisher that had already moved article drafting onto AI. The remaining bottleneck was me: every post still needed a featured image, and I was updating them by hand every day.

Image-generation APIs were too slow and too expensive to run on Lambda, so I composed the art instead. ChatGPT wrote the tagline and scored sentiment from the post; a Node canvas job layered branded templates, textures, and blend modes; WordPress REST uploaded the file as media.

Editorial stopped publishing empty-looking posts, and the designer went back to actual brand work. When a specific image missed, the next step was a WordPress plugin so they could regenerate one post without paging me.
tasks: Blueprint for a zero-touch AI content pipeline
Generating branded art on Lambda, not image APIs
Wiring OpenAI into headless WordPress publishing

name: How to improve page load times and Web Core Vitals
imageAlt: Article: improving Nuxt page load times and Core Web Vitals with preconnect, deferred embeds, and REST.
description: After a Nuxt redesign, I cut post-navigation load time 45% — preconnect, deferred embeds, and REST instead of GraphQL for above-the-fold post data.
dossier: After a two-month Nuxt redesign went live, Lighthouse and Core Web Vitals flagged FCP and Total Blocking Time on post navigation. I traced it to GraphQL on flagship pages, request waterfalls, and iframes that could not defer.

I preconnected fonts and the CMS origin so first-time visitors were not paying connection cost at render. Above-the-fold embeds — a live scanner SPA and an audio player — moved behind a delayed mount so they stopped competing with LCP.
Above-the-fold post data moved from GraphQL to REST, with a slug-to-ID dictionary for SPA navigation. Comments, tags, and related posts stay on GraphQL in onMounted. Initial load dropped about 45%.
tasks: Strategies to slash website load times
GraphQL and REST tradeoffs for Server Side Rendering
How to  protect and improve LCP and TBT
